result.reason: The operative language substantially reaches the preferred position: Company receives a 30-day written termination right covering active SOWs and a refund of prepaid post-termination fees, while Contractor cannot terminate when an SOW is outstanding. However, allowing Company to terminate “in part” exceeds what the playbook requires and creates uncertainty regarding partial-scope refunds. Drafting quality is also materially impaired by the unchanged lead-in stating that termination occurs pursuant to Paragraph 6, which conflicts with the new right in Paragraph 2(a), and by using “outstanding” without clarifying whether that means an active committed term.
